scenes.title: Administrator overview
scenes.speech: Welcome to Scout Storage. This administrator walkthrough uses the real application with demonstration data. Administrators manage inventory, accounts, requests, borrowing, maintenance, and reports.

scenes.title: Sign in
scenes.speech: Enter your administrator email and password, then select Sign in. The accounts shown here are demonstration accounts.

scenes.title: Storage overview
scenes.speech: The overview shows physical items, available stock, borrowed items, and maintenance. Review pending requests and overdue borrowing. These counts reflect recorded inventory activity.

scenes.title: Manage categories
scenes.speech: Administrators can add and edit categories. You can delete an unused category. Categories linked to existing equipment cannot be deleted.

scenes.title: Add equipment and a photo
scenes.speech: Enter an equipment name and select its category. Set Total stock and choose a photo from your computer. Saving creates individual physical items with separate codes, ready to borrow.

scenes.title: Edit equipment and total stock
scenes.speech: Edit equipment to update its description or photo, or increase Total stock. Increasing stock creates more physical items. Record individual item states instead of reducing stock and deleting history.

scenes.title: Add an item batch
scenes.cue: Equipment details → Add items → Review batch
scenes.speech: Open equipment details and add another batch. Choose the quantity and condition, review the generated codes, and confirm. Available and total counts refresh after the operation succeeds.

scenes.title: Item details and QR labels
scenes.speech: Each code identifies one physical item. Its page shows condition, borrowing history, and maintenance. Download and print the QR label to open this page. A phone needs a reachable website address rather than your computer’s localhost address.

scenes.title: Create users and assign roles
scenes.speech: Create a user and choose Administrator, Storage Keeper, or Scout. Passwords require at least twelve characters. These are the three supported roles; the Leader role has been removed.

scenes.title: Edit or deactivate an account
scenes.speech: Administrators can change account details, roles, and passwords. Deactivating an account blocks access and revokes existing sessions while preserving request and borrowing records. Reactivate it when appropriate.

scenes.title: Review requests
scenes.speech: Review requested equipment, quantities, and dates. Add notes when approving or rejecting. Approval does not hand over equipment. Issuing is a separate operation that checks availability again.

scenes.title: Issue an approved request
scenes.speech: Open Issue equipment from an approved request. Add the approved quantities to the cart and confirm. Selected items and the borrower must match the approved request.

scenes.title: Borrow multiple equipment types
scenes.cue: Borrowings → Issue equipment → Add to cart
scenes.speech: For direct borrowing, select the borrower, due date, and purpose. Add quantities from multiple equipment types to one cart. Review the item codes and confirm a single borrowing transaction.

scenes.title: Record a partial return
scenes.speech: Select only the items that have returned and record their condition. Other items remain borrowed. The borrowing stays partially returned until all items are resolved.

scenes.title: Select all and record condition
scenes.speech: Select all checks the remaining items for return. It does not automatically mark them lost. Good items become available, and damaged items enter maintenance. Mark Lost only for an item that is actually missing.

scenes.title: Complete maintenance
scenes.speech: Record the repair status, cost, and notes. When finished, choose the condition after repair and confirm whether the item should return to available stock. You can also retire it from service.

scenes.title: Reports and CSV export
scenes.cue: Reports → Apply filters → Export current page
scenes.speech: Reports cover inventory, borrowing, overdue items, damage, loss, and maintenance. Filter by category or dates. CSV export downloads the current displayed page, not every page of results.

scenes.title: Archive and audit history
scenes.speech: Archive equipment to preserve its history. Unresolved activity can prevent archiving. The audit trail records who made important changes and when they happened.

scenes.title: Sign out
scenes.speech: Select Sign out when finished to revoke your server session. Only administrators manage users and categories and access the audit trail.

scenes.title: Storage Keeper overview
scenes.speech: This walkthrough covers the Storage Keeper role: managing equipment and items, issuing and receiving borrowing, reviewing requests, maintenance, and operational reports. It uses demonstration data and computer-generated narration.

scenes.title: Sign in and review the overview
scenes.speech: Sign in using the account created by your administrator. Review available and borrowed items, pending requests, and overdue borrowing. User management and the administrator audit trail are not available to this role.

scenes.title: Add equipment and physical stock
scenes.speech: Storage Keepers can add equipment and upload a photo. Set the total number of physical items before saving. Borrowing requires available individual items with separate codes.

scenes.title: Manage individual items
scenes.cue: Equipment details → Item details → Edit item
scenes.speech: Open an item to review its code, serial number, and condition. Edit permitted details and notes. Change a borrowed item through the return workflow, and an item in maintenance through its repair record.

scenes.title: Review requests
scenes.speech: Approve or reject requests and explain your decision. Check the requested quantity and dates. Approval does not issue equipment or guarantee that stock will remain available.

scenes.title: Issue equipment with a cart
scenes.speech: Select the borrower and due date, then add equipment to the cart. Combine multiple equipment types, adjust quantities, or remove a row. Confirmation issues all selected items together if they remain available.

scenes.title: Record returns and select all
scenes.cue: Record returns → Select all → Record returns
scenes.speech: Open the borrowing when items arrive. Select all chooses only unresolved items. Review each condition and notes before saving. For a partial return, deselect anything that has not returned.

scenes.title: Report damage
scenes.speech: Open the individual item and select Report damage. Describe the problem. An available item moves into maintenance and cannot be borrowed until its repair is completed.

scenes.title: Repair and return to service
scenes.speech: Update the repair status, cost, and notes, then record completion. Choose the new condition and return it to available stock, or retire it. Do not complete a repair while the item is still outside the store.

scenes.title: Operational reports
scenes.speech: Review inventory, overdue borrowing, maintenance, damaged items, and lost items. Filter results and export the current page to a CSV file for daily follow-up.

scenes.title: Role permissions
scenes.cue: Categories: view only · No Users / Audit trail
scenes.speech: Storage Keepers can view categories but cannot create or delete them. User management and audit history belong to administrators. Ask an administrator when an account or category needs changing.

scenes.title: Sign out
scenes.speech: Sign out after work, especially on a shared computer. The Storage Keeper role handles daily operations and does not manage user accounts.

scenes.title: Scout overview
scenes.speech: Scouts can browse equipment, submit and track requests, view their own borrowing, and report damage to an item borrowed in their name. Scouts cannot manage inventory, issue equipment, or record returns.

scenes.title: Sign in
scenes.speech: Use the email and password provided by your administrator. There is no public administrator registration. After signing in, you see the functions permitted for a Scout.

scenes.title: Browse equipment
scenes.speech: Browse equipment to see available quantities and other item states. Open equipment details to see individual items and codes. Scouts cannot add equipment or change stock.

scenes.title: Request multiple equipment types
scenes.speech: Create a request with the required start and end dates and purpose. Enter a quantity for each equipment type, then submit. A request does not reserve stock or automatically create a borrowing.

scenes.title: Track request decisions
scenes.cue: My requests → Request details → Status history
scenes.speech: Open your request to review its status, decision notes, and history. You can see only your own requests. Approval accepts the request; an administrator or Storage Keeper records the handover separately.

scenes.title: Cancel a request
scenes.speech: Cancel your own pending or approved request before equipment is issued. Enter a reason and confirm. You cannot cancel another person’s request or change an approval decision yourself.

scenes.title: Your borrowing and due date
scenes.speech: Open your borrowing history to see the items issued to you and their due date. Review each item’s state and any recorded return date. Administrators and Storage Keepers record equipment handover and returns.

scenes.title: Report damage to your borrowed item
scenes.speech: If an item borrowed in your name is damaged, open that item’s page and select Report damage. Give a clear description. Scouts can report only their own currently borrowed items. The item stays borrowed until staff record its return.

scenes.title: Follow your damage reports
scenes.speech: The maintenance page shows the damage reports you submitted. Storage Keepers and administrators update repairs, costs, and return items to stock. Scouts do not have repair completion controls.

scenes.title: QR labels and your account
scenes.speech: An item’s QR label opens its details page and does not grant additional permissions. Your account page shows your name, email, and role. Ask an administrator to change account details or reset your password.

scenes.title: Sign out and return equipment
scenes.speech: Sign out when finished. Other users’ private records are outside your permissions. To return equipment, hand it to the Storage Keeper so they can record the return and each item’s condition.
